parakeet: The idea of a messiah, whether nationalistic or universal, Jewish or Christian, is not just outdated, it's toxic to human equality. Because any worldview that says one group is chosen, one figure will rule all, one person's pain redeems the world, and one kingdom deserves to crush the rest, isn't offering hope. It's offering holy hierarchy. And that should offend your sense of justice, your dignity as a human being, and your commitment to a world where no one has to bow, bleed, or beg to be seen as worthy. The problem isn't just Jesus, it's the job description. Because even if someone did fulfill every Messianic prophecy, even if they conquered the nations, punished the outsiders, and restored their chosen people to glory, that wouldn't be a triumph of righteousness. It would be the rise of a God who governs by apartheid, a messiah who segregates humanity into insiders and infidels, demands obedience instead of understanding, rewards tribal loyalty over universal dignity, and punishes people for the crimes of their ancestors and calls conquest a divine right, is not a redeemer. They are a theological tyrant with a robe and a PR team. This isn't salvation. This is supremacy and sacred packaging. And the fact that billions still long for a figure like this, still kneel for one, still teach their children to wait for one, that shouldn't comfort us. It should terrify us. Because if your hope depends on someone else being conquered, if your freedom requires someone else's submission, if your peace is built on someone else's silence, then what you're waiting for isn't a savior, it's a master. And there's nothing holy about that.
